facts.text: Loma Grande was originally inhabited by nomadic Coahuiltecan Indian groups who lived as hunter-gatherers prior to European contact.
Spanish expeditions in the late seventeenth century documented abundant wildlife, including buffalo, throughout the Loma Grande region.
Loma Grande developed as a sparse farming settlement during an agricultural boom fueled by artesian wells and railroad expansions.
The terrain around Loma Grande consists primarily of brushland and low-relief grasslands modified by historical ranching and farming.
Loma Grande features a semi-arid climate with hot summers, mild winters, and an average annual temperature of around seventy-two degrees.
Loma Grande sits at an average elevation of five hundred eighty-four feet within the undulating topography of Zavala County.
